name: PT Bakrie & Brothers Tbk

frontmatter.title: Bakrie & Brothers: a toll road inside a family holding company, priced as if the discount were absent
frontmatter.summary: BNBR is what the Bakrie family's vehicle has become since buying the Cimanggis-Cibitung toll road: a motorway to 2061, a large listed EV stake, and steel and digital businesses worth less than book. Earnings are one-off, the first half of 2026 was a loss, the family funds itself by issuing shares, and the shares trade near the marked value of the parts, so the call rests on the holding-company discount the control warrants. We initiate at Reduce.
thesis: Only two parts of this group carry a mark that is not book: the Cimanggis-Cibitung toll road, at the fair value the company's own acquisition accounting put on it, and the listed VKTR stake, at market; net of a negative book residual for every other business they clear the traded price by only a sliver, so the call rests on the holding-company discount the governance warrants rather than on the marks alone.

Almost all of the value that reaches the parent is one asset's cash flow, and the debt that finances it sits on the group: the project syndicated loan alone is a multiple of the toll road's net asset value, and the first half of 2026 ran at a loss because the floating-rate interest landed before the revenue ramped.

Reported profit is not a guide: FY2025 earnings were carried by a one-off bargain-purchase gain on the toll road acquisition, FY2024 by gains on loan settlements and asset sales, and the accumulated deficit was erased by a quasi-reorganization, so the earnings history cannot anchor a multiple.

Every cross-check that treats the shares as a claim on a stable base is unusable: the equity was reset by that quasi-reorganization, the share count in the data pack is contradicted by the audited statements, and the company has issued shares repeatedly, most recently a rights issue struck above book.

Governance is the discount's DNA here: control sits behind offshore vehicles, the float is a minority, the group transacts with affiliates across the family's other listed companies, and the related-party balance sheet is large, so the discount widens rather than narrows without a dated catalyst, and we do not see one.

The honest bull case is that the concession runs to 2061 and the traffic is beating its own budget, so a house-card valuation of the motorway rather than its acquisition mark, plus a tariff increase and the EV order book, would close much of the gap to the price.

catalysts.event: Third-quarter report, the first balance sheet to carry the July rights issue and its debt repayment
The 2026 toll tariff adjustment on the Cimanggis-Cibitung section
Full-year 2026 results, with the first clean read on whether the group covers its interest
Annual shareholders' meeting and any decision on the accumulated-loss position and a dividend

blocks.text: We initiate coverage of PT Bakrie & Brothers at **REDUCE** with a target of **Rp41** against a last price of **Rp54**, a total return of **-23.3%** [S0]. The call is not a view on Indonesian infrastructure demand, which is real and which this company's toll road is directly exposed to; it is a view on what the listed parent actually owns and what it is worth.

Three things set the file. First, the group rises or falls on one operating asset and one large listed stake. The Cimanggis-Cibitung toll road, the section of the Jakarta outer ring road network that completes it that was consolidated on 28 November 2025, carries a concession to 2061 and was recognised in the group's own acquisition accounting at identifiable assets of **15,896** less identifiable liabilities of **11,579** [S18, S12]; alongside it sits the listed VKTR stake, which on a market mark is the larger of the two parts. Everything else the company owns, once that stake is carved out, leaves the parent with negative book value, because most of the rest of the group's equity sits behind the non-controlling interest that consolidation creates [S12]. Second, the toll road's debt is the group's debt: the project syndicated loan alone is **9,715** [S12], and the company itself attributes the loss it posted in the first half of 2026 to the floating-rate interest on that toll road arriving before its revenue ramped [S5]. Third, the profit history is not a history of profits: FY2025's result is dominated by a **320** one-off gain on the bargain purchase, and the accumulated deficit was extinguished by a quasi-reorganization in 2024 [S11, S12].

A holding company trades at a discount to the value of the assets it controls, and that discount is
not an anomaly to be arbitraged: it is the normal state of affairs, and it persists because the
minority shareholder cannot force the value out. It narrows when something happens that deliberately
moves cash or ownership towards the parent's shareholders, so the reason to expect a narrower
discount is that a dated event will change it, not that the discount exists.

What moves the value? The tariff schedule on the motorway and the traffic that runs over it; the interest rate the group pays on the loan that financed it, which is floating; and whether the manufacturing, electric-vehicle and digital businesses ever earn their cost of capital, which at present they do not [S3, S5]. Against that, the price already assumes that all three go right.

BNBR is the listed vehicle through which the Bakrie family holds a set of industrial and infrastructure businesses. The company describes itself as a multi-sector investment holding company and reports three segments: infrastructure and manufacturing, fabrication and construction services, and trading, services and investment [S12]. Its largest businesses by revenue in FY2025 were the steel structure, pipe and construction group PT Bakrie Metal Industries, which contributed **2,200**, and the electric-vehicle group PT VKTR Teknologi Mobilitas Tbk, which contributed **1,080**; the infrastructure business PT Bakrie Indo Infrastructure contributed **464**, and the digital-infrastructure arm PT Multi Kontrol Nusantara, whose revenue rose by about a sixth to **359**, runs a fibre and homepass network under government connectivity programmes [S2]. The footprint is domestic: the toll road is in Greater Jakarta, the steel and pipe businesses serve oil, gas and infrastructure customers from Bekasi, and the electric-vehicle assembly plant is in Magelang [S15].

The business that matters is the toll road. PT Cimanggis Cibitung Tollways operates the section between the Cimanggis and Cibitung junctions as part of the outer ring network, with a concession running to 10 August 2061 and a possible extension beyond it; it has been fully operational since 2024, and traffic in the eight months to August 2026 averaged **43,911** vehicles a day, above the company's own budget, on revenue of **2,500** per day [S15, S18]. The group took its ownership of the concession from a tenth to full control on 28 November 2025, buying out PT Sarana Multi Infrastruktur and PT Waskita Toll Road, and taking over the shareholder loans those two had extended to it [S12, S18].

The rest of the group is smaller and thinner than its revenue suggests. The steel, pipe and construction businesses sell into oil and gas and into public infrastructure; Bakrie Autoparts, now held through the electric-vehicle arm, supplies automotive components to original-equipment manufacturers; VKTR assembles electric buses for TransJakarta and states that it is the only supplier meeting the domestic-content requirement for the twelve-metre fleet [S2, S15]. There are also early-stage businesses in rooftop solar and electric-vehicle charging through Bakrie Power and Helio Synar Energi, and a three-dimensional construction printing venture with a Danish partner [S2].

Control is family-based and indirect. The company's stated controlling shareholders are Aburizal, Nirwan Dermawan and Indra Usmansjah Bakrie, holding through a chain of vehicles, and the largest single registered shareholder in the corporate structure is an offshore company holding **26.0%**; the free float is **30.0%** [S11]. BNBR is therefore a holding company in the strict sense: what its shareholders own is a claim on subsidiaries that are themselves controlled by the family, and what those shares are worth is the ability to extract value from those subsidiaries.

The sectors BNBR operates in are not one industry, and the house treats it as a conglomerate rather than as a company in any of them. The macro backdrop is a balance-of-payments pressure regime under which the division tilts towards export-supply-discipline names and away from Indonesian rate-sensitive domestic demand, which is the wrong side of the tilt for a group whose largest business is a domestic toll concession and whose balance sheet is floating-rate [S0].

The toll road is where the industry question actually lives, and it is a regulated-concession business rather than a competitive one. The concession sets the tariff and the term; the value comes from traffic growth over a period long enough that the early years of debt service do not determine the outcome. Cimanggis-Cibitung is the final section of the outer ring network, connecting the Soekarno-Hatta airport corridor to the Tanjung Priok port hinterland, and it competes for traffic with the Jakarta inner ring and with the Jakarta-Cikampek corridor [S15]. It is a toll road in a densely populated catchment, and its own traffic is running above both its internal budget and the company's comparison set of similar roads [S15]. That is a genuinely good asset.

The rest of the group competes in industries where it is a challenger rather than a leader. The steel-pipe and fabrication business sells into oil and gas and into infrastructure spending; the automotive-components business sells to vehicle manufacturers and is exposed to domestic purchasing power; the electric-vehicle business depends on a public-policy-driven procurement stream and on domestic-content rules [S2, S15]. None of them has the pricing power of a concession, and their combined contribution to the group's profit is not visible as a separate, positive parent-attributable number [S12].

Regulation and policy are therefore the dominant external influences. Toll tariffs are set by the regulator, so the timing of an adjustment matters more than any commercial decision the operator makes; the electric-vehicle business depends on government procurement and on local-content rules; and the group's infrastructure and connectivity contracts are awarded by the state [S15]. The macroeconomic influences are the rupiah, which determines the cost of the dollar-denominated portion of the group's borrowing, and the floating-rate environment, which the company singled out when it explained why its first half of 2026 was a loss [S5].

On a five-forces reading, the toll road has a negligible threat of new entry and no substitute within its corridor, which is why it is the only part of the group worth close to its carrying value; the manufacturing and components businesses face import competition, fragmented customers and modest switching costs, and their returns reflect that. The moat, in one sentence, is the concession document, and it belongs to one subsidiary: the group cannot replicate it, its competitors cannot attack it, and every other business in the group has to earn its keep against one. That is the whole of the competitive advantage. [S12, S15]

FY2025 revenue was **3,743** on a consolidated basis, slightly lower than the prior year, and the audited statements show why the reported profit should not be read as earnings power. Gross profit of **744** left an operating profit of only **117** after operating expenses of **628**, so essentially the entire profit for the year came below the operating line [S12]. That below-the-line result includes a gain of **320** on the bargain purchase of the toll road, foreign-exchange and asset-sale gains, and the reversal of a receivable provision, net of interest and financial charges [S12].

Depreciation and amortisation is one line where the data pack is wrong. The audited notes show **171** of depreciation and amortisation for FY2025 allocated between the cost of revenue and general and administrative expenses, where the pack carries only the latter; restating it, and the operating lines with it, takes FY2025 EBITDA to **288** [S12, F6]. The operating lines are restated the same way: the pack's operating expenses and operating profit came from a different allocation than the filing's Total Beban Usaha and LABA USAHA, which leave FY2025 operating expenses of **628** and an operating profit of **117** [S12, F52, F54]. The pack's share count is wrong as well: the audited statements show **173,417**m shares in issue at the end of FY2025 rather than the larger number the pack carries, and every per-share figure here is struck on the post-rights total that filed count grosses up to under the July 2026 rights issue, not on the pack's number [S12, F8].

Our forecast carries the toll road's first full year. FY2026E revenue of **5,165** is a step of about two-fifths on FY2025, because the toll road was consolidated only from the end of November and the first half of 2026 alone produced **2,590** of revenue, with the company attributing the growth to the toll road's consolidation and to electric-vehicle sales [S3, S5]. We hold the gross margin at the reported first-half ratio of about a quarter of revenue rather than FY2025's lower figure, and we hold operating expenses at the reported first-half ratio, a little over a seventh of sales, because the FY2025 ratios were struck on a revenue base less than half the size and a haircut to the reported ratios would be an unexplained caution [S3]. EBITDA on that basis is **821**, a margin of **15.9%** against FY2025's **7.7%** [S0, S12].

The forecast then shows the file's central problem. Interest expense is struck on opening debt at about **6.5%** a year, the first-half 2026 rate annualised, and that interest bill is larger than the operating profit the group generates in every forecast year, so the model runs small losses throughout: net profit to the parent is **-431** and stays negative [S0, S5]. The company's own explanation of the first-half loss is the same arithmetic: the floating-rate interest on the toll road landed before its revenue ramped [S5]. Working capital is a further drag, because the group carries operating working capital at a little under two-fifths of revenue, largely related-party, so growth consumes cash rather than releasing it [S0].

Two limitations of this projection must be stated. It gives no credit for the July 2026 rights issue: the engine's cash-flow template has no line for an equity issuance, so the capital action that raised the equity and repaid group debt cannot be shown as one movement, and the repayment is carried in the valuation bridge instead [S5, S16, S19]. Interest expense is therefore struck on a debt balance about **4,362** too high for the years after the repayment, and the losses we show are wider than the post-issue reality; nothing in the rating depends on it, because the call is set by the sum of the parts and the cross-checks rather than by the projected profit and loss account. Separately, the forecast funds the group's cash deficit and rolling maturities with new borrowing at the last actual's scale rather than with a dated facility, which is a stated financing assumption rather than a sourced plan [S0, S12].

Capital allocation has run one way for years: towards the family's other vehicles, and towards issuing shares. The equity has been enlarged by a series of capital increases, and the accumulated deficit stood at a level that required a quasi-reorganization in 2024, which eliminated **19,530** of accumulated losses and reset the comparability of the equity and earnings history [S11, S12]. Dividends have not been paid in the period covered by the price history, and the policy makes any future payout conditional on financial condition and a shareholders' resolution [S6].

The house method for a conglomerate values it on its parts, because a consolidated multiple applied to a group like this one measures the largest subsidiary and calls it the whole. We build the sum of the parts from three things, and label each with the method behind it: the toll road at the fair value the company's own acquisition accounting put on it, the listed VKTR stake at market, and everything else at book.

The toll road is carried at the group's share of the price its own November 2025 business combination put on it: identifiable assets acquired of **15,896** less identifiable liabilities assumed of **11,579** less the non-controlling-interest portion leaves net assets acquired of **4,101** [S12, F12, F13, F44]. That is the one third-party mark on a group asset, and it is the company's own.

VKTR, the listed electric-vehicle subsidiary, is carried at market, because the method card requires a listed stake to be marked to it. BNBR holds the shares, an economic interest of **24.4%** at the last balance-sheet date [S12, F49], and the entitlement it transferred into VKTR's own rights issue fixes the holding at the twelve-for-thirty-five ratio [S25, F37]; the stake is marked at the IDX theoretical ex-rights price of **675** a share against the cum price of **835** [S23, F38, F39]. That mark is worth several times the book value it replaces. It is taken at the theoretical ex-rights price rather than the cum one because VKTR's own rights issue diluted non-participating holders by up to **25.5%** [S25, F51].

Everything else - the steel and pipe group, the components business, the digital-infrastructure and power businesses - is carried at book, and stated as such. That residual line is negative: consolidated parent equity of **3,853** less the toll road's group share and less the VKTR book value leaves less than nothing, because the rest of the group's book equity is largely the non-controlling interest's and the operating businesses carry accumulated losses [S12]. It is book, not a house-card valuation of those businesses, and the bull case is precisely that they are worth more than book. We flag it as the least-verified line in the file.

Two post-balance-sheet items go into the bridge. The July 2026 rights issue raised **4,760** from **89,920** new shares at **53** each, which adds that equity to net assets; of the proceeds **4,362** repaid in full the facility the group's subsidiary owed to Hartman International and Bank Nobu, and the balance funded working capital, the BCI construction capital, the CCT rest-area equity and company operations [S16, S19, F42]. The first half of 2026 ran at a loss, which subtracts from them [S15, F43]. Because the group's own debt sits inside each part's net asset value, no further deduction is made for it and the remaining debt is disclosed in the parts. A holding-company discount of **33%** is then applied, taken at the middle of the band house sums-of-parts discounts persist in rather than at a narrow end, because this file carries the things that keep such discounts wide: control behind offshore vehicles, a minority float, a quasi-reorganization that reset the equity, and repeated issuance [S11, S12].

The primary method produces **Rp39** per share [S0]. The cost of capital inside the model is high and is meant to be: with the group's debt-to-equity at **1.56** the levered beta is **2.00**, the cost of equity is **19.2%** and the weighted average cost of capital is **12.0%** [S0]. That is what a holding company with a floating-rate debt load and a single operating asset should be discounted at, and it is not the constraint on the valuation; the marks are.

The cross-checks are set on the peer median rather than on this company's own five-year average, and the override is stated in the assumptions with its reason. The data pack's own-history multiples are struck on a share count the audited statements contradict and on an equity and earnings series that the quasi-reorganization reset and that the bargain-purchase gain inflates, so they are not a benchmark for today's net assets [S11, S12, F8]. On the peer median, the P/E leg produces **Rp28** per share and the P/BV leg produces **Rp28** [S0]. Both sit below the primary, and the divergence is itself the message: the multiple legs capitalise a book equity the quasi-reorganization reset and a net profit the one-off bargain-purchase gain inflates, so neither is independent evidence about the marked value of the parts.

What today's price implies is the clearest statement of the gap. Held to our marks on the parts, the reverse of the primary method says the traded price is consistent with a holding-company discount of only **7.3%**, against the **33%** we think the governance and the history warrant [S0]. In other words the market is already paying close to the full sum of the parts rather than a discount to them, so a buyer at this price is not being paid to accept the family-control discount at all; they are paying for the option that the toll road is worth far more than its acquisition mark, that the electric-vehicle business becomes profitable, and that the group's other assets are worth more than book.

One housekeeping note on the market data: the data pack's own market-capitalisation line is struck on the pack's share base rather than on the post-rights count, so it is carried here only as an unadjusted engine figure and no per-share mark in this report rests on it [S0].
The risks are concentrated and mostly correlated, which is itself the point.

**Interest and refinancing (high likelihood, high impact).** The group's operating profit does not cover its interest expense in any year of our forecast, and the company attributes the first-half 2026 loss to the floating-rate interest on the toll road [S5]. A further rise in the rate the syndicated lenders charge, or a failure to refinance on comparable terms when the current agreement runs, moves the equity directly. The facility's amendments extended its term and reset its rate following the change of control, which tells the reader that the lenders, not the company, set the terms [S12].

**Governance and related-party gravity (high likelihood, medium impact).** The controlling family holds through offshore vehicles and the float is a minority [S11]. The group transacts with affiliates, holds short-term investments in the family's other listed companies, and has repeatedly used equity issuance as its funding instrument, most recently a rights issue struck above book [S12, S16, F27]. Each of those is a channel through which value can reach the family before it reaches the minority.

**Concentration (medium likelihood, high impact).** One asset dominates, one concession, one corridor. The sum of the parts is the toll road and the listed VKTR stake against a negative residual for everything else, so an adverse toll outcome cannot be diversified away inside the group [S12].

**Earnings quality (observed, not prospective).** The FY2025 result is dominated by a one-off gain and the FY2024 result by gains on loan settlements and asset sales; the accumulated deficit was eliminated by a quasi-reorganization; and the share count in the data pack is wrong [S11, S12]. A reader who anchors on the reported multiple is anchoring on a distortion.

**Equity issuance and liquidity (high likelihood, medium impact).** The rights issue relieved the near-term cash problem by moving a large part of the equity into new hands: it was struck at **53** a share, it diluted a holder who did not subscribe by up to **34%**, and the two largest holders transferred their entitlement to a standby buyer rather than fund it themselves [S16, F27, F28, F50]. A family that funds itself from the equity rather than from cash flow dilutes its minority holders a little every cycle, and the enlarged share count is now the base for every per-share figure here [S12, F8]. The same pattern has just run at VKTR, whose own rights issue diluted non-participating holders by up to **25.5%** [S25, F51].

The scenarios are mirrored and shock the same three drivers both ways. In the bear case the holding-company discount widens, revenue growth is cut and the cost of debt rises, which together give **Rp37** at **25%**; the base case gives **Rp41** at **50%**; and in the bull case the discount narrows, growth is better and the cost of debt falls, giving **Rp46** at **25%** [S0]. The bull is not decorative: the toll road's traffic is already ahead of the company's own budget, the section carries a concession to 2061 with the prospect of a five-year extension and a planned tariff increase in 2026, and its Burangkeng interchange adds connectivity to the Jakarta-Japek South road [S15, F17, F18, F36]. A house-card valuation of that motorway rather than its acquisition mark is what the bull is buying. The bear is that mirror plus the dilution already struck: the discount stuck wide, the group still loss-making once the equity has been spent, and holders permanently diluted [S16, F50]. The asymmetry worth naming is the one the method card insists on: a narrower discount requires a dated catalyst that moves value to the parent's shareholders, and on the evidence in this file - a rights issue already done, no dividend record, and a family that has historically funded itself from the equity - we cannot date one.

Signposts that would change the view: a tariff adjustment materially above the scheduled one, a visible reduction in the group's debt once the rights-issue repayment is filed, a concrete and dated plan showing the manufacturing and electric-vehicle businesses earning their cost of capital, or any transaction that upstreams cash towards the parent's shareholders rather than away from them.

Ownership and control are the heart of the file. The company's ultimate beneficial owners are the three Bakrie brothers, identified through direct holdings that are microscopic in themselves and through indirect chains; the corporate structure shows the largest registered shareholder at **26.0%**, with the public holding **30.0%** below the disclosure threshold [S11]. Control is therefore not proportionate to economic ownership in any simple sense, which is the classic condition in which holding-company discounts persist rather than close.

Related-party dealings are structural rather than incidental. The group holds short-term investments in PT Bakrie Sumatera Plantations, PT Darma Henwa, PT Bakrie Telecom, PT Bakrieland Development and PT Energi Mega Persada, each of which it describes as an affiliate under common control of the same shareholders and boards, and the audited statements note that related-party terms may differ from those available with third parties [S12]. That disclosure is exactly what a minority holder should weigh when the residual value of the group is negative and the operating companies are small. On pledged shares and board composition, the audited statements and the annual report in the record do not quantify pledges, and we report that as not established rather than as a clean bill [S11, S12].

The dividend record is the honest quality metric. There is no dividend in the price history and none in the audited period; the policy makes any payment conditional on financial condition and a shareholders' resolution, and the last decision on record was to carry profit to retained earnings [S6]. A holding company that neither distributes nor earns enough to cover its own costs is one whose discount has nothing to pull against it.

The equity history is the governance issue with teeth. The audited statements show a sequence of capital increases through non-preemptive rights and conversions, and a quasi-reorganization in 2024 that eliminated **19,530** of accumulated deficit, resetting the equity and loss history so that the company's own comparability across years is gone [S11, S12]. The July 2026 rights issue continued the pattern [S16]. On ESG, the integrated annual report carries the group's sustainability framework; nothing in the record suggests an ESG exposure that changes the valuation, and we do not pad the section to imply otherwise. [S11]

The dated catalysts are in the frontmatter: the third-quarter report, which will be the first balance sheet to carry the rights issue and the debt repayment and therefore the first clean read on the group's leverage; the 2026 toll tariff adjustment on the motorway section; the full-year 2026 results, which will show whether the group covers its interest before exceptional items; and the annual meeting, where the accumulated-loss position and any dividend decision sit [S7, S15, S6]. We also watch the interest rate charged on the syndicated facility at each amendment, the traffic and revenue per day the company reports for the toll road against its own budget, and whether the data-centre intention the company has aired becomes a filed, dated and funded project rather than a story [S2, S12].

The KPIs we monitor between updates are the traffic and daily revenue of the toll road, the group's interest cover, net debt as a multiple of EBITDA, the parent-attributable residual after the non-controlling interest, and the share count, which is the number a minority holder should watch most closely in this name [S0, S12].

bear.narrative: The toll road's floating-rate debt service keeps running ahead of its ramping revenue, the group stays loss-making and has to keep funding itself with new debt, and the discount stays at the wide end of its range rather than narrowing; the manufacturing and EV businesses are marked at zero rather than at book, and the listed VKTR stake is marked down from its theoretical ex-rights price.

bull.narrative: The tariff increase and the Jakarta-Japek South interchange lift toll traffic faster than plan, the EV assembly business converts its TransJakarta order book into a profit and the group's parts are marked at their house-card values rather than at book, and the cost of debt falls as the post-rights structure settles.

sensitivity.title: 12-month value vs holding-company discount and cost of equity

assumptions.label: Revenue growth
assumptions.basis: FY2026E carries the full-year consolidation of the CCT toll road, which entered the group only on 28 November 2025: first-half 2026 revenue of 2,590 (F24) already matches two-thirds of the whole of FY2025, and the company attributes the step to the toll road plus electric-vehicle sales [S15, S5]. Because that is a scope change and not a growth trend, the series steps down to a single-digit rate from FY2027E and holds at the house terminal rate thereafter. [S5, S12]

assumptions.label: Gross margin at base input costs
assumptions.basis: Held at the reported first half of 2026 (25.1% of revenue) and not at FY2025's 19.9%, because FY2025 held only one month of a toll road whose gross margin is far above the manufacturing average; the toll road alone ran at a 846 revenue and 694 EBITDA in FY2025 on a standalone basis (F33, F34), so weighting the parts lifts the blended margin, and a haircut to the reported ratio would be an unexplained caution [S3, S12, S22]. Held flat after FY2026E: no disclosed contract or tariff schedule justifies a further step.

assumptions.label: SG&A / revenue
assumptions.basis: Held at the reported first-half 2026 ratio (about 14.2% of revenue) rather than FY2025's 16.8%, which was struck on a revenue base less than half the size of the one the toll road now brings, and because the first-half 2026 income statement already carries the operating expenses of that mix. The 16.8% is the audited ratio: Total Beban Usaha of 627.521 on revenue of 3,742.973 (F54, F52, S12). No cost programme is disclosed that would take it lower.

assumptions.label: D&A / revenue
assumptions.basis: Restated from the audited notes: depreciation and amortisation of 171.363 for FY2025 (F6) against the data pack's 22.921, which is the general-and-administrative allocation only; the charge now also carries the toll road's concession amortisation, so the ratio is set above the FY2025 audited ratio of 4.6%. [S12, F6]

assumptions.label: Capex / revenue
assumptions.basis: Held at the reported first-half 2026 run-rate: capex of about 182 in the half against revenue of 2,590, with the toll rest area, the EV assembly facility and the steel businesses still consuming capital; no archived source discloses a taper. [S15, S5]

assumptions.label: Operating working capital / revenue
assumptions.basis: Held at the FY2025 ratio (operating working capital of 1,453.9 on revenue of 3,743.0), which is the last audited figure for a group whose receivables are heavily related-party. [S0]

assumptions.label: Effective tax rate
assumptions.basis: Set above the FY2025 reported rate of 3.1%, which is distorted by non-taxable bargain-purchase and restructuring gains, and at the low end of the Indonesian corporate range because the group carries tax losses forward after the quasi-reorganization. [S12, S11]

assumptions.label: Cost of debt (on opening debt)
assumptions.basis: The audited FY2025 statements disclose long-term loans at annual rates of 3%-10% (Rupiah) and 1%-7% (US dollar), with the toll road's 9,715.210 syndicated facility (F15) the largest single line and the 2.5% post-rights BTI facility the newest, so the blended cost sits in the middle of that band [S12, S19, F15]. That is consistent with the first half of 2026, the first period to carry the toll road's debt for a full six months: the company posted a net loss of 217 against an operating profit of 301.53 (F43, S3), which leaves room for a net financing cost of roughly five hundred in the half, an effective rate near 6.5% on opening debt of 16,748. This is the first-half rate annualised; it is not the FY2025 ratio, which was struck on a debt balance a fraction of the current one. [S12, S3, F43]

assumptions.label: Yield on opening cash
assumptions.basis: Set below the disclosed time-deposit rates of 5.0%-6.25% (and 6.75% at end-2025, F48) to allow for the working balances the group keeps outside term deposits, rather than fitted to the first-half interest income. [S12, F48]

assumptions.label: Net new borrowing
assumptions.basis: The rights issue itself is carried in the valuation bridge, not here: the engine's corporate cash-flow template has no line for an equity issuance, so the July 2026 capital action cannot be shown raising cash and repaying debt without driving the modelled cash balance negative - the debt and P&L lines this forecast touches are therefore stated on the pre-issue basis and the repayment is carried in the bridge [S5, S16]. What this line does carry is the funding the continuing business needs: a group that consumes operating cash, pays no dividend and has no equity instrument left funds its deficit and rolling maturities with debt, so the base case assumes it refinances, which is why the modelled cash balance stays non-negative rather than going to minus five thousand as an unfunded forecast would. No specific new facility is disclosed beyond the rest-area borrowing already inside capex, so this is a stated financing assumption at the last actual's scale, not a dated plan. [S5, S12, S19]

assumptions.label: Other non-operating items
assumptions.basis: Held at zero in every forecast year. FY2025's other income of 401.969 is dominated by the 320.127 one-off gain on the CCT bargain purchase (F14) plus foreign-exchange and asset-sale gains, and the company's own statement that the first half of 2026 ran at a loss because of the toll road's floating-rate interest says the repeatable line is not there. No archived source forecasts a further one-off. [S12, F14, S5]

assumptions.label: Minorities' share of net profit
assumptions.basis: Set at 2% against the audited FY2025 ratio of 1.77%, reflecting the large non-controlling interest the consolidation carries (818.494 at 31 December 2025, of which 812.291 is VKTR, F45) and the fact that minorities absorb their share of the group's losses. [S12, F45]

assumptions.label: Dividend payout
assumptions.basis: Zero. The company has paid no cash dividend in the period covered by the price history and its stated policy makes any payout conditional on financial condition, positive retained earnings and a shareholders' resolution; the last decision on record was to carry profit to retained earnings, and the group has just raised equity rather than returned it. [S6, S5]

assumptions.label: Change in share count
assumptions.basis: FY2026E carries the July 2026 rights issue at its filed terms: 14 new Series E shares for every 27 old, which is 0.5185185185 of the count in issue at the last filed balance sheet (F8, F9) [S16, S5]. The ratio is the exact filed one and reconciles the forecast share vector to the pro-forma total of 263,336.672m in F8; nothing is assumed after that.

assumptions.label: Terminal growth (DCF)
assumptions.basis: House terminal growth for an Indonesian rupiah reporter: long-run nominal GDP, no company-specific claim. [S0]

assumptions.label: Holding-company discount to SOTP
assumptions.basis: Set at 33%, a discount level chosen inside the 20-40% band the method card says a family holding company's discount persists in, and taken at the house holdco-discount-narrowing archetype's range rather than at a narrow end. The 0.33 is a chosen discount level, not the archetype's probability of the discount narrowing: the 'rate' field in data/base_rates.yaml is that success probability, and we do not read it as the discount itself. The discount is applied and not narrowed: the method card makes the discount the base rate rather than the opportunity, and this file carries the flags that keep a discount wide - a controlling family whose stakes sit behind British Virgin Islands vehicles (F32), a public float of 29.98% (F31), serial equity issuance that has repeatedly reset the share count, and a quasi-reorganization that eliminated 19,530 of accumulated deficit in 2024 (F30) [S11, F30, F31, F32]. BNBR's own five-year discount history cannot be computed here - no house sum-of-the-parts exists before this file - so the archetype base rate is used rather than a name-specific range, and a discount narrower than it needs the dated catalyst the method card demands, which this file, on the evidence, does not have beyond the rights issue already done.

challenges.challenge: The two-entry SOTP is not an SOTP: CCT at Rp4,317.18bn plus the negative residual at minus Rp463.58bn equals FY2025 parent book equity of Rp3,853.17bn exactly. That means every residual-segment value, holdco debt outside CCT, acquisition funding and minority/NCI effect is allocated by subtraction rather than independently valued. VAL_HOLDCO_DISCOUNT requires listed stakes at market and unlisted segments on their own house cards, with holdco opex and net debt separately bridged.
challenges.answer: The SOTP is now built from three independently marked parts, not a residual plug: the toll road at the group share of the acquisition fair value (identifiable assets F12 less liabilities F13 less the non-controlling-interest portion, i.e. F44), the listed VKTR stake at market, and every other business carried at book as an explicit residual; holdco_net_debt is 0 with its basis stated because each part is entered net of its own liabilities. The two-entry identity that summed to parent equity is gone.

challenges.challenge: VKTR is a listed subsidiary but is hidden inside the negative residual book plug rather than marked as ticker x market price. The method card expressly says listed stakes use market value. This is independently material because the minority interest is Rp818.494bn at end-2025, largely the VKTR minority, and the negative residual is the main evidence offered that non-toll operations subtract value.
challenges.answer: VKTR is now a separate listed-stake row marked at market: the IDX theoretical ex-rights price F39 against the cum price F38, on the holding fixed by the entitlement transferred into VKTR's own rights issue (S25, F37) and its 24.40% economic interest (F49), with the book value it replaced removed from the residual to avoid double counting. A new fact F51 records the VKTR rights dilution, which is why the theoretical rather than the cum price is the mark.

challenges.challenge: All per-share marks combine inconsistent dates: the bridge adds the full July 2026 rights-issue proceeds of Rp4,760bn to NAV, but SOTP, P/E and P/BV divide by the 30 June 2026 issued count of 173,416.832509m shares. Adding 89.92bn shares gives approximately 263.337bn shares, about 52% more. The error directly inflates SOTP, NAV/share, TP and market-cap math.
challenges.answer: share_change is now the exact filed ratio, 14 new Series E shares for 27 old (0.5185185185, S16), giving a forecast share vector of 263,336.671585m from the 173,416.83m filed count (F8); the SOTP denominator, every per-share leg and the report language now use that single post-rights count, and the stale sentence that divided the marks by the last filed count is removed. mcap_rep stays the engine's pack market-cap line computed on the pack's share base (an engine artifact we cannot edit), but it is not cited in the report and does not drive the rating, which rests on the per-share SOTP.

challenges.challenge: The forecast is mechanically impossible after the July rights issue: net_borrowing is zero through FY2035, debt stays at Rp16,748.334bn, and interest stays at Rp1,088.642bn while cash goes from Rp549.554bn to minus Rp115.617bn and minus Rp717.104bn. The draft admits interest is on a debt base roughly Rp4,760bn too high from FY2027E and that no equity issuance/debt repayment can be represented. An explicitly negative cash balance is not a conservative modelling convenience.
challenges.answer: The forecast no longer runs to a negative cash balance: net_borrowing is now a positive, stated financing assumption that funds the group's cash deficit and rolling maturities at the last actual's scale, so modelled cash stays non-negative. The July capital action itself is carried in the valuation bridge, and section 3 states explicitly that interest is struck on a debt base about F42 too high for the years after the repayment, and that the losses shown are wider than the post-issue reality.

challenges.challenge: The bridge claims Rp4,760bn of group-debt relief, but the archived material-transaction filing says funds received were Rp4.362417779559bn and that this exact facility was used to repay all principal owed by BTI to Hartman and Bank Nobu. Rp4.76tn is gross rights-issue proceeds, not external debt extinguished; the balance was allocated to working capital, BCI construction capital, CCT rest-area equity and company operations. S19 is archived but never cited in facts, assumptions or the report.
challenges.answer: The bridge label is decomposed: it carries the Rp4.76tn of equity the July rights issue raised as the net-asset addition, and states that Rp4.362tn of it (F42, verbatim in S19) repaid in full the BTI facility owed to Hartman International and Bank Nobu, the balance funding working capital, BCI construction capital, CCT rest-area equity and operations. S19 is now cited in the bridge, in post_bs_review and in report section 4.

challenges.challenge: The multiple_source override rejects own-history because the pack share count is contradicted, the quasi-reorganization reset equity and the bargain gain distorts earnings. But the quasi-reorganization was an intra-equity elimination/reclassification, not a reduction in net assets; the overridden peer median also uses the same wrong pre-rights share count and a mixed post-balance-sheet bridge; and the peer set mixes toll, coal, auto, multifinance and retail names. The justification therefore rejects own history for the wrong reason and accepts a peer median without showing business comparability.
challenges.answer: The quasi-reorganization is now described correctly - an intra-equity elimination of the accumulated deficit, not a reduction in net assets (F30) - and the override still gives its reason. On the peer median: it is computed from the peers' own data packs, so BNBR's share count does not enter it; and the peer set is the house CONGLOMERATES comparator group (ADRO, DSSA, CUAN, ASII), every one a listed parent valued on its parts, with the absence of a toll or EV peer stated as a limit on the legs rather than hidden.

challenges.challenge: Base FY2026E gross margin rises from 19.9% to 25.1% and the opex ratio falls from 19.6% to about 14.2%, justified only by saying a lower ratio would be an unexplained caution. Scope alone does not prove the assumed full-year blended rates: the toll road's revenue/cost mix, concession amortization and central costs are not quantified, and H1-2026 is not necessarily representative because interest landed before revenue ramped. The QCEBITDA-margin gap is +11.0pp.
challenges.answer: The FY2026E ratios are set at the reported first-half 2026 blend (S3, F24, F25), and the step is scope, not margin expansion: FY2025 held only one month of a toll road that ran at F33 revenue against F34 EBITDA on a standalone basis, far above the manufacturing average, so weighting the parts lifts the blended FY2026E margin. The same basis is the qc_justifications entry for the calibration flag. The bulk of the step is the toll road's entry, disclosed, not an assumed margin gain.

challenges.challenge: The cost inputs are inconsistent with the lender and balance-sheet evidence: cost_of_debt of 6.5% is an H1 estimate while the FY2025 LK shows Rupiah facilities at 3%-10%, USD facilities at 1%-7%, a 7.0% Bank Nobu acquisition facility, and a 2.5% post-rights BTI facility; cash_yield of 6.0% is set against H1 interest income rather than disclosed deposit terms; and the 33% discount is asserted as the base rate without BNBR's own five-year discount history.
challenges.answer: The cost inputs are rebuilt from the filing: cost_of_debt sits in the middle of the disclosed facility band (3-10% Rupiah, 1-7% US dollar) with the 2.5% post-rights BTI facility (F41, S19) the newest line; cash_yield is lowered to 5.5%, below the disclosed term-deposit rates (F48), rather than fitted to first-half interest income; and the discount basis states plainly that no BNBR-specific five-year SOTP history exists to range against, so the archetype base rate is used instead. The post-rights debt cost is the F41 facility plus the CCT syndicated loan (F15).

challenges.challenge: S17 is archived under BNBR but is an IDNFinancials report about suspected Cs-137 contamination in footwear from an unrelated factory at Cikande. It does not mention BNBR, Bakrie, toll roads, steel, EVs or any group company; initials NM do not identify the group. Retaining an irrelevant radioactive-contamination source in a BNBR packet creates false provenance and suggests an unexamined external risk.
challenges.answer: S17 is removed from the registry and the sources directory; no paragraph in the report ever cited it, so there is no provenance to reconcile. The remaining set is company filings, the integrated annual report, investor presentations, a regulator disclosure and press, each cited where it is used.

challenges.challenge: The bull case captures neither the disclosed tariff review nor concession economics: traffic is already 3.25% above budget, revenue is Rp2.5bn/day and 3.02% above budget, the tariff increase is planned for 2026, and the concession runs to 2061 with a possible five-year extension. A credible toll DCF could be worth more than the acquisition-date net-asset mark, especially with the Burangkeng/Japek interchange connectivity cited in the company presentation.
challenges.answer: The bull case now names the toll economics: the planned 2026 tariff increase, traffic already above the company's own budget (F18, F36), a concession to 2061 with a possible five-year extension (F17) and the Burangkeng interchange connectivity to Jakarta-Japek South (S15), and section 5 carries the resulting range. We do not build a separate toll DCF and say so: no tariff schedule or traffic forecast is archived, so the upside is shocked through the drivers rather than fitted to numbers the record does not carry.

challenges.challenge: The downside omits post-rights dilution and control economics: the rights were issued at Rp53 while the market traded around Rp98 in late August; major holders transferred rights to a standby buyer; the public faced up to 34.15% dilution; and the model itself projects negative parent profit every forecast year, negative FCFE and eventually negative cash. A price-only bear scenario does not capture existing holders' permanent per-share dilution or refinancing risk.
challenges.answer: A dilution-aware bear is added: F50 (34.15% maximum dilution of a non-participating BNBR holder, S16), F51 (25.53% for VKTR holders, S25), the rights price F28, and the two largest holders transferring their entitlement to a standby buyer (S16, F27). Section 5's equity-issuance risk and the bear narrative now carry permanent per-share dilution alongside the refinancing and negative-FCFE risks, and section 3 discloses the negative projected parent profit and the new-borrowing funding assumption.

challenges.challenge: The share_change input is 0.518484, but 89,920m divided by 173,416.832509m is 0.518519447. The forecast share series is therefore 263,330.685496m instead of approximately 263,336.832509m. The 6.147m difference is small, but share count is a load-bearing input and the report claims every per-share figure is exact to the audited filing.
challenges.answer: share_change is corrected to the exact rights ratio: 14 new shares for 27 old is 0.5185185185, not 0.518484. The forecast share vector is now 263,336.671585m and reconciles to F8's pro-forma total.

challenges.challenge: The bridge includes a minus Rp225bn H1-2026 loss sourced only to S0, which is not a registered archive source. The loss is material to NAV and no operating fact supports its amount. Using an unregistered source identifier violates the evidence standard even if the number is plausible.
challenges.answer: The bridge H1-2026 adjustment is now sourced to a registered archive source: F43 (the company's own 6M26 investor update, S15) carries the consolidated net loss of Rp217bn, and the report cites S15/F43 rather than the data pack. The -225bn figure and its S0 provenance are gone.

challenges.challenge: The scenarios cite probabilities of 25/50/25 but shock only the discount by +/-10pp and revenue growth by +/-3pp. Those shocks do not mirror the one-off bargain gain, interest-rate exposure, related-party drag, traffic/tariff outcomes or dilution; and no evidence supports assigning only 25% to the bear case when the model itself shows negative profit, negative FCFE and negative cash. The resulting bear/base/bull range is compressed around a deeply negative call.
challenges.answer: The scenarios now shock three mirrored economics drivers - the holding-company discount, revenue growth and the cost of debt - and the narratives name the real drivers (tariff and traffic for the bull, dilution and a discount stuck wide for the bear), with F50 cited for the dilution. Probabilities stay 25/50/25 with the base at half, per MOST_LIKELY_BASE_CASE. Section 5 states plainly that the call does not rest on the discount narrowing, because no dated catalyst exists, so the base case is not an optimistic artefact.

missing_bull_case.note: The draft admits the toll road is a genuinely good asset, traffic is above budget, revenue is Rp2.5bn/day, the term runs to 2061 with a possible extension, and a 2026 tariff review is near, yet none of this enters a traffic/tariff/concession-length upside or a house-card toll valuation; the bull merely trims the same wide discount and revenue.

missing_bear_case.note: The draft does not price the downside once all 89.92bn new shares are outstanding, including dilution from Rp98 to Rp53, the standstill buyer absorbing unsubscribed shares, refinancing/covenant risk on the Rp9.715tn syndicated loan, related-party leakage, negative FCFE and cash going negative in the model, and operating-profit shortfall if traffic or tariffs disappoint.

assumption_realism.note: The three value levers are CCT's mark, residual-group value and share count/discount. The CCT mark uses acquisition-date identifiable net assets rather than an operating DCF; the residual is a negative book plug rather than a segment valuation; and NAV is divided by the pre-rights share count while including post-rights cash. Interest and cash use an artificial zero-borrowing constraint.

evidence_and_citations.note: Spot checks verified the CCT identifiable amounts, H1 revenue/EBITDA, concession date, traffic, segment revenue, rights-issue plan and share count. But S17 is an irrelevant Cs-137 footwear source that no paragraph cites; S17/S19 expected post-issue and repayment facts are absent; and Rp4.362tn external repayment is misreported as Rp4.76tn debt relief.

valuation_method_fit.note: VAL_HOLDCO_DISCOUNT requires listed stakes at market, unlisted parts on their own house cards, look-through earnings/leverage/upstream coverage, and a dated narrowing catalyst. The file provides one acquisition-based toll mark plus a negative book residual, no VKTR market mark, no house-card residual valuation, no look-through bridge, and no named dated catalyst.

bias_and_tone.note: The tone understates rather than overstates the bear case in one mechanical respect: the pre-rights denominator materially overstates SOTP and TP per share while the overstated interest materially understates earnings. The admissible outcome may be even more negative; the call cannot rest on the present arithmetic.

consistency_with_sector_deck.note: The draft correctly uses the CONGLOMERATES holdco_sotp template, macro deck, holdco archetype inputs and domestic-cycle exposure; the defect is not deck selection but the SOTP construction, missing look-through and post-rights capitalization.

conservatism_audit.note: Gross margin, opex and D/A rise against FY2025 without disclosed rate/volume proof, but the larger departures are optimistic, not cautious: the SOTP and all per-share cross-checks use too few shares; the bridge credits Rp4.76tn rather than Rp4.362tn external debt relief; residual book excludes value-checks on sunk development capex; and the bull requires growth/discount improvement without sourcing.

calibration.note: Two QC BLOCKs were marked justified, not cured. The EBITDA-margin step is a scope change, but interest/debt are still projected on the wrong pre-repayment base, cash goes negative in the forecast, and LTM cross-check inputs are stale. The extreme-call justification explains sentiment, not a verified reverse-SOTP as of the October price.

signoff.notes: Every FATAL/MATERIAL red-team challenge (C1-C14, five FATAL) and every QC round-2 finding is answered on substance: the SOTP is rebuilt as three independently marked parts (CCT at the group share of the acquisition fair value F44, the listed VKTR stake at market F39, the residual other businesses at book, flagged as the least-verified line), the per-share marks use the single post-rights count 263,336.672m, and the FY2025A/FY2024A opex/ebit are restated from the audited P&L (F52-F55) so the calibration base is correct. The report reconstructs to the printed target (NAV 58.26/share x 0.67 = sotp 39.03; blend 34.75 x 1.1918 = 41.4). lint PASS, QC round 2 PASS, blocking gates empty. Batch bias check: the industry is mixed (ASII/IMJS BUY, ADRO HOLD, DSSA/CUAN SELL, BNBR REDUCE), so there is no systematic one-sided tilt to explain. The lean on this name is sourced per name and not a shared input applied inconsistently against the industry's other parts-based names: the 0.33 holdco discount sits inside the VAL_HOLDCO_DISCOUNT 20-40% band and is justified by this name's own governance flags (control behind offshore vehicles, minority float, a 2024 quasi-reorganization that reset the equity, repeated dilutive issuance) rather than the 0.30 used for ADRO/CUAN/DSSA; terminal growth of 0.04 matches the domestic names (ASII/IMJS), not the coal holdcos' 0.02; and the VKTR mark at the IDX theoretical ex-rights Rp675 rather than the cum Rp835 is the correct post-dilution mark after VKTR's own dated October 2026 rights issue (S25, F51). The cost-of-capital outliers (WACC 11.98%, COE 19.18%, highest bar IMJS) carry a stated reason (high floating-rate D/E, single operating asset). The auditor's too_bearish read is supported, not a blocking defect. Approved for publication.

bias.note: Round 2. The aggregate view still leans pessimistic, though materially less than at round 1, and every remaining departure is sourced rather than a defect. The -23.3% call rests on applying the 33% base-rate holdco discount to a marked NAV of Rp58.26/share that the market itself prices only about 7.3% below (engine reverse-DCF implied discount 0.073, fund record), i.e. a ~26pp widening with no narrowing credit; and the listed VKTR stake is marked at the IDX theoretical ex-rights price of Rp675 (F39) rather than the observed cum price of Rp835 (F38), about 19% lower. Both are sourced - the 33% is the house base rate mandated by the VAL_HOLDCO_DISCOUNT card (discounts of 20-40% persist indefinitely by default; 'the discount is the base rate, not the opportunity'), and the ex-rights mark is the correct post-dilution mark after VKTR's own dated October 2026 rights issue (S25, F51). The element that drove round 1's too_bearish is now fixed - the mis-scoped P/E leg (-69% versus the SOTP primary, off the pack's wrong LTM) is re-priced to -27.3%, inside the 30% cross-check divergence tolerance with no engine warning (checks.warnings empty), which lifted the target from ~37 to 41.4 and the rating from SELL to REDUCE. No unsupported optimism either - the FY2026E ratios take the reported first-half 2026 actuals and the full Rp4.76tn rights proceeds are bridged at probability 1.0, both disclosed. The lean is therefore reduced and supported, not a blocking defect.

recomputed.item: FY2025A net debt (debt 16,748.334 incl leases - cash and short-term investments 1,557.818)

findings.finding: FY2025A EBIT/EBITDA do not reconcile to the audited consolidated statements, and the calibration base is therefore wrong. The model builds FY2025A on the data pack's operating expenses of 733.848 (EBIT 10.536, EBITDA 181.90), but S12's consolidated statements of profit or loss show Total Beban Usaha (operating expenses) of 627.521 and LABA USAHA (operating profit) of 116.863 for FY2025 (2024: 586.605 / 282.872). Correct FY2025A EBITDA is 116.863 + D&A 171.363 (F6) = 288.23, so the model understates it by 106.3, or 37%, an unexplained gap far beyond the 5% tolerance. The analyst restated cogs, da, interest, shares and equity from the filing but left the wrong ebit/opex pack figures in place; the report and the calibration qc_justification further assert that the audited year shows '19.6% of revenue going out as operating expenses' cited to [S12], where the filing shows 16.8%. The engine's only BLOCK flag (calibration.ebitda_margin) is raised on this distorted base.
findings.answer: Restated FY2025A and FY2024A from the audited consolidated statement of profit or loss as facts keyed by line name - operating profit ebit 116.863 / 282.872 and total operating expenses opex 627.521 / 586.605 (F52-F55, S12) - so the engine now rebuilds FY2025A EBITDA at 288.23 (116.863 plus D&A 171.363, F6) instead of the pack's 181.90 and the calibration base is correct. The flagged gap narrows from +11.0pp to +8.2pp (FY2025A margin 7.7% against FY2026E 15.9%), still scope-driven from the toll road's entry and justified in qc_justifications. The wrong 19.6% operating-expenses figure is corrected to the filing's 16.8% in the opex_pct basis, the report and the calibration justification. The restated ebit also moves the engine's LTM basis off the pack's mis-scoped trailing year, so the P/E cross-check now capitalises the last audited actual and the rating re-prices to REDUCE at a target of 41.4; every sentence that depended on the pack number is rewritten.

findings.finding: F8 (bs_shares 2026Q3 = 263,336.671589m) is cited to S12, but S12's issued-and-fully-paid capital note shows 173,416,832,509 shares at 31 December 2025 and contains no 263,336,671,589. The post-rights total is a derived pro-forma (173,416,832,509 x 41/27), not a filed count in S12; the value is arithmetically correct but its stated provenance and its '2026Q3' label do not match the source. The market-cap reconciliation itself holds: the SOTP, every per-share leg and nav_per_share divide by the 263,336.672m post-rights count.
findings.answer: F8 is relabelled as a COMPUTED PRO-FORMA, not a filed count: the base count of 173,416,832,509 shares at 31 December 2025 (F9, S12) grossed up by the filed July 2026 rights ratio of 14 new Series E shares for every 27 old, i.e. 41/27 (S16, F27). The misleading 30 June 2026 base date and the 2026Q3 period label are corrected to the audited 31 December 2025 base and a 2026Q3E pro-forma label; no numeric change. The market-cap reconciliation holds - the SOTP, every per-share leg and nav_per_share divide by the 263,336.672m post-rights count.

findings.finding: The analyst's flag is confirmed: mcap_rep = 10,876.398 = Rp54 x 201,414.782m, the stale data pack share base (restated to 173,416.833m for the history but never to the post-rights 263,336.672m). It is an engine artifact, is not cited anywhere in fund record, and the per-share SOTP and multiple legs all divide by 263,336.672m, so the rating does not rest on it.
findings.answer: Accepted as an engine artifact, with the footnote the finding asks for. mcap_rep (Rp54 times the pack's 201,414.8m share base) is computed by the engine's market block before the balance-sheet restatement and cannot be edited from the analyst side; it is cited nowhere in fund record and no per-share mark rests on it. Section 4 now states plainly that the pack's market-capitalisation line is carried as an unadjusted engine figure struck on the pack's share base, not the post-rights count. No action on the rating.

findings.finding: The 0.33 holdco_discount is taken from the fund record 'holdco_discount_narrowing' field 'rate' (the archetype's probability of the discount narrowing), which happens to sit inside the method card's 20-40% discount band; the basis sentence presents the archetype probability as if it were the discount itself. The level is defensible but the stated derivation is not.
findings.answer: Reworded. The 0.33 holdco_discount basis now states it is a discount LEVEL chosen inside the 20-40% band the method card says family holdcos persist in, taken at the discount-narrowing archetype's range rather than at a narrow end, and explicitly NOT the archetype's 0.33 probability-of-narrowing field in data/base_rates.yaml. The report's section 4 sentence is reworded to match and now prints the discount through the engine placeholder. The 33% level itself is left in place per MOST_LIKELY_BASE_CASE, sourced to the method card and the name's governance flags.

findings.finding: Round-1 BLOCK resolved and independently verified from the archived filing. Facts F52-F55 carry verbatim S12 quotes (audited consolidated statement of profit or loss, p.15 - "Total Beban Usaha 627.521 586.605 Total Operating Expenses LABA USAHA 116.863 282.872 OPERATING PROFIT", confirmed by grep). The restored FY2025A EBITDA of 288.23 (ebit 116.863 + D&A 171.363) and FY2024A of 398.00 (282.872 + 115.127) each reconcile revenue 3,742.973 -> gross profit 744.384 -> less opex 627.521 -> ebit 116.863 -> plus D&A, and the FY2025A debt of 16,748.334 matches the filing's short-term 1,836.563 + current maturities 345.747 + long-term 14,557.479 + lease liabilities 8.545. Every load-bearing number reconciles within 5%; the engine BLOCK calibration flag is now justified (gap narrowed +11.0pp -> +8.2pp) and blocking is empty.

The SELL-to-REDUCE re-pricing the restatement triggered is coherent and traceable.
